newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Honduras rejects extradition of Haitian colonel.
newsitem.headline: Honduras rejects extradition of Haitian colonel.

text.p: Honduras on Wednesday rejected a request to extradite ex-Haitian police chief Col. Joseph Michel Francois to the United States on grounds of drug-running.

"The judge in the case has acquitted my client and thrown out the extradition request to the United States. The judge did not find him guilty of any of the charges leveled against him," the colonel's attorney Francisco Lagos told reporters.

Francois, the former police chief of the Haitain capital Port-au-Prince during the 1991-1994 military government, was arrested on March 7 in San Pedro Sula, a sultry Honduran industrial city to the north of the capital.
U.S. drug agents had hoped to extradite him to Miami to stand trial but the move was hampered by Honduran legal procedures.

The U.S. Attorney General's indictment against Francois said he placed Haiti's military and political hierachy under his control to ship thousands of pounds of cocaine and heroin to the United States in league with Colombian drug barons.

Francois was believed to have been the mastermind behind the September 1991 coup that toppled President Jean-Bertrand Aristide. He became the capital's police chief and created a network of plainclothes policemen known as "attaches" who instigated a reign of terror against opponents of the regime.
